question: On a Mercator world map Greenland looks about as big as Africa. How many Greenlands would really fit inside Africa?
answer: About 14. Africa covers some 30.4 million km² and Greenland 2.17 million. Mercator's map stretches everything away from the equator, four times in area at 60° and far more near the poles, so Greenland swells. Boston's schools moved to an equal-area map in 2017 partly for this reason.
move: Before comparing sizes on a map, ask what the projection preserves.
ask: Which map have I used to judge a size it was never meant to show?

options.label: Just 1
options.note: That is the map talking: Mercator inflates Greenland near the pole.

options.label: About 3
options.note: Still far too few: Africa is about 30 million km², Greenland 2.2.

options.label: About 50
options.note: Too many: Greenland is still bigger than Mexico.

source: Florida International University News, on Boston's switch of world map, 2017
